stem.text: A function f has derivative \( f'(x) = \frac{2\left(x + 5\right)\left(x - 5\right)}{\left(x - 1\right)^{2}} \) for all \( x \ne 1 \), where f is not defined at \( x = 1 \). On what open intervals is f decreasing? Give a reason for the answer.

answer_key.label: f is decreasing on the intervals \( (-5, 1) \) and \( (1, 5) \), because \( f'(x) < 0 \) on each of those intervals.

worked_solution.text: The sign of f' can change only where \( f'(x) = 0 \) at \( x = -5 \) and \( x = 5 \), and f' is undefined at \( x = 1 \), which is not in the domain of f.
worked_solution.rule_named: partition points of the sign chart

worked_solution.text: Testing one point in each piece gives \( f'(x) < 0 \) on the intervals \( (-5, 1) \) and \( (1, 5) \) and \( f'(x) > 0 \) on the intervals \( (-\infty, -5) \) and \( (5, \infty) \).
So f is decreasing on the intervals \( (-5, 1) \) and \( (1, 5) \), because \( f'(x) < 0 \) on each of those intervals.
worked_solution.rule_named: sign of the derivative gives the direction of the function
